prompt:
You are a senior typographer and information designer. You lay out data tables for publication. You judge layouts by looking at the rendered result as a whole: what the table is for, how a reader scans and compares it, which columns belong together or play the same role, proportion and rhythm across columns, a clear hierarchy of headers and groups, whether rows read as units, whether words, numbers and identifiers stay intact, and how text and white space are distributed. Fewer lines or a shorter table is not automatically better, and neither is equal widths or symmetry; decide case by case and say why.

Table: [val] Income statement · fiscal quarters (language en).
Grid: 6 columns × 6 rows. Row headers: yes (first logical column identifies each row).
Merged cells: "USD millions" spans 1 col × 2 row; "Fiscal 2024" spans 4 col × 1 row; "Full year" spans 1 col × 2 row.
Per-column content facts (content px at 15px font, excluding padding):
  col 1: header "USD millions" · longest unbreakable word 94px · one-line width 409px
  col 2: header "Fiscal 2024 › Q1" · longest unbreakable word 38px · one-line width 38px
  col 3: header "Fiscal 2024 › Q2" · longest unbreakable word 41px · one-line width 41px
  col 4: header "Fiscal 2024 › Q3" · longest unbreakable word 40px · one-line width 40px
  col 5: header "Fiscal 2024 › Q4" · longest unbreakable word 40px · one-line width 40px
  col 6: header "Full year" · longest unbreakable word 48px · one-line width 61px
Each column also has 21px of padding+border, so a column given width w px shows w−21 px of text.
Available width: 360px (the dashed pink box = the reader's viewport). The column widths you choose must sum to at most 359px.
This table cannot fit without splitting words at 360px. You MAY choose a total wider than 359px (the reader then scrolls horizontally), or squeeze and accept splits — a design decision.
Rendering convention: the screenshot always shows the WHOLE table. Anything beyond the dashed box is not clipped; it is the part a reader reaches by scrolling sideways, so judge both what fits in the box at first sight and the cost of scrolling to the rest.
Fixed: content, font, 15px font size, padding, borders, colours, alignment. You control ONLY the column widths.

The image shows the table's content with every cell on one line, so you can read everything. Study it first.
1) Understand it: what is the table for, how will people read, scan and compare it, which columns play the same or similar role, which values must stay intact, which text may wrap naturally, and where existing row height could absorb wrapping.
2) Propose 3 genuinely different column-width designs for 360px (different strategies, not small variations).
Reply ONLY JSON: {"understanding":{"purpose":"","reading":"","groups":["columns that belong together and why"],"keep_intact":[""],"may_wrap":[""]},"designs":[{"name":"A","widths":[int px per column, column 1 first],"idea":"one sentence"}]}

log.raw: {"understanding":{"purpose":"Compare fiscal 2024 income-statement measures across four quarters and the full year, in USD millions.","reading":"Readers scan each labeled row across to compare quarters and the annual total, and scan down a column to compare measures within a period. Row labels need enough space to remain recognizable as units.","groups":["Q1–Q4 are parallel periods and should have equal widths to support comparison.","The full-year column summarizes the same measures across the four quarters and needs room for its longer heading.","The first column identifies each measure and needs more width for descriptive labels."],"keep_intact":["Quarterly and full-year numeric values, including decimal points.","Quarter identifiers Q1–Q4.","Individual words in row labels where space permits."],"may_wrap":["Long row labels can wrap at word boundaries, especially the cost-of-revenue label.","The Full year heading can wrap between words.","The existing two-level header provides height for wrapped header text."]},"designs":[{"name":"A","widths":[145,62,62,62,62,82],"idea":"Give labels room to wrap naturally and keep the quarter columns equal and numeric values intact, with horizontal scrolling to reach the later periods."},{"name":"B","widths":[110,49,49,49,49,53],"idea":"Fit the viewport with equal quarter widths, accepting splits in long label words and potentially in numeric values for a compact overview."},{"name":"C","widths":[250,62,62,62,62,82],"idea":"Prioritize readable row labels with a generous first column while preserving equal quarter widths, at the cost of more horizontal scrolling to compare periods."}]}
